name: Western Dihedral

waypoints.name: Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)
waypoints.note: ~4 hours trailhead-to-base, then Class 4 scrambling via Skeena26's base to reach this route.
waypoints.directions: Take I-5 to the Arlington exit, then follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. Out of Darrington, follow Squire Creek Road until a washout gates it; the parking area is at that closure. Nothing beyond is driveable, so park there and continue on foot up the old roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing.

waypoints.name: Grassy saddle (South Face routes)
waypoints.note: Climbs the obvious reddish right-facing corner visible from the saddle; crux liebacking/stemming and a finger traverse on pitches 2-3.
waypoints.directions: Walk the old Squire Creek roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing to two cut logs, one on either side of the road, with old logging cable visible, and turn right there onto a well-beaten boot track. It drops to a ford of the creek, then climbs steeply through old growth, steep and dirty near the top, into open grassland and the main grassy saddle at the foot of the South Face, about three hours from the car.

approach_variants.name: Squire Creek trail, cut logs, ford and the grassy saddle
approach_variants.notes:
From Darrington take Squire Creek Road to the washout that gates it, then walk the old roadbed past the flagged landslide crossing.

The South Face turn-off is two cut logs, one either side of the road, with old logging cable visible — turn right there onto the well-beaten boot track. It drops to a ford of the creek, then climbs steeply through old growth, steep and dirty near the top, into open grassland. The main grassy saddle bivy is about three hours from the trailhead, with a second smaller saddle roughly ten minutes further west along the wall.
hazards: Steep dirty forest on the upper boot track
Hand-drilled bolts of unknown age on the face sections
approach_variants.baseFinding: Get to the right saddle first. The main grassy saddle sits at the start of Concerto in C for Drill and Hammer and is the reference every South Face line is described from; the smaller saddle ten minutes west is a different camp. From the saddle the grey granite apron of the South Face is in front of you and the individual lines are picked off it. This route takes a dihedral with a lieback/stemming crux on pitch 2 and a delicate smearing finger traverse on pitch 3, sandwiched between easier friction above and below — so easy friction on pitch 1 is correct here, not a sign you are on the wrong line. Protection is a mix of hand-drilled bolts on the faces and gear in the dihedral and cracks; a face with no gear placements at all is not this route. The sources consulted do not give a ground-level marker specific to this line beyond the wall and the saddle reference — confirm against the wall topo before committing.

approach: South Face is another wall within the same Squire Creek Walls complex as Waterfall Basin, reached via the same Darrington-area approach: I-5 to the Arlington exit, SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington, then Squire Creek Road to the washout-blocked parking area. From there, follow the same rough, unmaintained approach — the old roadbed past a landslide crossing, a faint trail through streambed and alder brush, a ford of Squire Creek, and obscure forest track — before breaking into the open basin roughly 2 hours from the car; South Face is one of the walls encountered within that same basin complex, with route-finding (flagging, cairns) required in several spots.
